concept: PasswordInput is the same recessed window as Input, made for a secret. A round key stands beside the well and latches down to show the characters, and the window prints the word for the state it is in, so a person never has to guess whether anyone can read the screen.
family_difference: PasswordInput adds a latching show and hide key beside the well, prints the word hidden or shown inside it, and can print a strength line, where Input is a plain text window.

default_to_avoid.pattern: password input with an eye icon inside the field that swaps between an open and a struck-through eye and changes only its colour
default_to_avoid.why_not: An icon that alone carries the state leaves people guessing which of the two pictures means shown, so dial prints the word as well and latches the key.

default_to_avoid.pattern: password input strength meter drawn as a red to green bar
default_to_avoid.why_not: A bar that is told by colour alone fails people who cannot see the hue and invites the unit's orange, so the strength is a printed word under the well.

references.source: system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a latched key beside a window, the window printing which band is in use
Input lab round (apps/lab/input/sheet.png, pick A): the well, label and messages are inherited unchanged

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The well is surface.sunken with elevation.well like Input, so the secret reads as cut into the body and the key beside it as the part that moves.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The show and hide key is an IconButton at control.md (control.lg at size lg), a 44px disc, and it stands outside the well so it never overlaps the characters.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: The key is a real button that Tab reaches and Space or Enter latches, with aria-pressed telling a screen reader whether the characters are shown.

derivation.consequence: the legend is the control's value made visible
derivation.form: The word hidden or shown is printed inside the well after the characters, so the key's state is read in plain words as well as on the latched key.

derivation.consequence: every state still has its shape, word or mark
derivation.form: Shown is told by the lock glyph opening, the printed word changing and the key latching, three cues that survive a grey screen.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The latched key is neutral glass, the strength line is ink with a word, and nothing in the field uses the unit's orange.

variants.reason: PasswordInput follows Input, which was derived in its own round with three lab candidates and picked A; the well, label and messages are the same, and only the latching key, the state word and the strength line are new, so no new candidates were rendered.

root.why: The field stacks its label, row and messages in one column so the label sits on the inset line above the well.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the printing beside every other part of the unit.

row.why: The well and the key share one row with a module gap, so the key stays beside the secret and a thumb finds it at the end of the line.

well.why: The recess takes the inverse light, shade on its top-left inner edge, so the person sees where the secret goes.

field.why: Typed characters are primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks, and the field fills the whole well so its press area is 44px tall.

word.why: The printed word hidden or shown sits beside the characters in secondary ink above 4.5:1, so the state is read without relying on the glyph or the colour of the key.

key.why: The show and hide key keeps a 44px hit area and a real button role, so it is reachable by finger, keyboard and screen reader.

strength.why: The strength line is printed under the row as a word in secondary ink and sits in a polite live region, so a change is read out and never told by colour alone.

md.why: The default well is 44px tall beside a 44px key, the smallest target that every part in dial keeps for a finger.

lg.why: A 52px well with larger text beside a 52px key for the main field of a phone sheet, where a thumb needs more room.

focus-within.why: The well shows the same dark ring as every part when its input holds the keyboard focus.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid well draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below names the problem with a glyph.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled field loses its recess shadow and fades to half, so it reads as not taking input right now.

data-readonly=true.why: A read-only field keeps the recess and the ink so the secret stays copyable, but the cursor stops asking for typing.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well keeps a real border and the focus ring uses the system highlight colour.
